input: Write a due diligence memo on Revolut

team.claim: Nik (Nikolay) Storonsky — Co-founder & CEO since 2015; previously an emerging-markets equity derivatives trader at Credit Suisse and Lehman Brothers; owns more than 25% of Revolut directly or indirectly.
Vlad Yatsenko — Co-founder (CTO per company materials; listed as Non-Executive Board Member on the About page); previously software engineering at UBS and Deutsche Bank.
Victor Stinga — Chief Financial Officer (interim CFO as of July 2024 per Reuters; confirmed CFO in the 2025 annual report).
Martin Gilbert — Chair; co-founded Aberdeen Asset Management (1983), led its 2017 merger with Standard Life; former deputy chairman of Sky plc and chairman of FirstGroup.

Béatrice Cossa-Dumurgier appointed CEO of Western Europe (Paris HQ) in June 2025; ex-McKinsey and French Finance Ministry, 15 years at BNP Paribas (COO Retail Banking, CEO Personal Investors), COO of BlaBlaCar and Believe, left the Société Générale board to join.

Sid Jajodia — Chief Banking Officer, overseeing all Revolut banking entities from the London global HQ; Joe Heneghan leads the Lithuanian-licensed European bank; Francesca Carlesi heads the UK business.
Regional executives: Paroma Chatterjee CEO Revolut India; Juan Miguel Guerra CEO Revolut Bank Mexico; James Gibson head of Revolut Business; Antoine Le Nel Chief Growth & Marketing Officer.
CEO Storonsky changed his residence from the UK to the UAE (Companies House filing shows the change in October 2024); Revolut declined to comment on the reason.

Notable recent departures: dozens of employees left Revolut Business sales roles in the UK and other European offices in November 2026 amid performance reviews; the company denies layoffs, calling the exits routine.

Board includes Michael Sherwood (retired Vice Chairman and co-CEO of Goldman Sachs International), Caroline Britton (18 years audit partner at Deloitte), Ian Wilson (ex-RBS, Santander UK, Tesco Bank, Monzo CRO), John Sievwright (20 years at Merrill Lynch) and Dan Teodosiu (ex-Google, Microsoft; former CTO of Onfido).

output.company: Revolut (Revolut Group Holdings Ltd, London, UK; principal operating entities Revolut Ltd, Revolut Bank UK Ltd, Revolut Bank UAB)

funding.claim: July 2021: $800 million Series E led by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and Tiger Global, valuing Revolut at $33 billion.

August 2024: secondary share sale providing employee liquidity at a $45 billion valuation, led by Coatue, D1 Capital Partners and existing investor Tiger Global, with Morgan Stanley as sole placement agent; made Revolut Europe's most valuable private tech company (company claim).

November 2025: secondary share sale completed 24 Nov 2025 at a $75 billion valuation (up 66% from $45B), led by Coatue, Greenoaks, Dragoneer and Fidelity Management & Research, with participation from NVentures (NVIDIA), Andreessen Horowitz, Franklin Templeton and T. Rowe Price; fifth employee share sale.

November 2026: secondary share sale completed 4 Nov 2026 valuing Revolut at $115 billion (up 53%), led by Glade Brook Capital Partners, Coatue, Durable Capital Partners, T. Rowe Price Associates and Baillie Gifford; brought no new money into the company and the amount of stock sold was not disclosed.

IPO timing: Storonsky says an IPO will not happen before 2028; reports suggest a possible listing valuation of $150-200 billion, with a dual Nasdaq/London listing considered and a preference for a primary US listing; no public registration statement or prospectus found on SEC EDGAR or the FCA NSM as of Oct 26, 2026.

output.verdict: Revolut is a genuinely high-growth, profitable fintech — FY2025 revenue of $6.0B (+46%) with $2.3B pre-tax profit, 68-80M customers, and a $115B private valuation backed by Coatue, Fidelity, T. Rowe and Baillie Gifford — and its 2026 banking launches (UK, Mexico, Australia, NZ, OCC conditional approval for a US charter) materially de-risk its licence strategy. The closer looks are (1) a repeated AML/data-security record — the €3.5M Lithuanian AML fine plus three prior fines, the 2022 breach of 50,150 customers and the September 2026 accidental data disclosure — against the backdrop of the UK's highest fraud-complaint volumes, and (2) a valuation that has risen 3.5x since 2021 purely through employee/investor secondaries with no new capital, a founder who relocated to the UAE, and an IPO pushed to no earlier than 2028.

business.claim: Revolut sells retail and business financial services: accounts on tiered plans (free Standard up to Ultra at ~£60/month), money transfer and currency exchange, cards, savings, credit (loans, credit cards, BNPL), stocks/automated investing, insurance, crypto, plus add-ons like eSIM mobile plans and airport lounges.

Business model is diversified and largely fee-based: 2025 revenue mix was card payments 22.2%, interest income 21.6%, subscriptions 15.7%, wealth 14.7%, FX 13.4%; fee-based revenues were 76% of total turnover and Revolut Business 16% of total income.

Operates in ~40 markets and is a licensed bank in 30+ of them (including UK, most of the EEA, Mexico); in the US Revolut is not a bank — cards are issued by partner banks (Lead Bank, Cross River Bank, Sutton Bank) with Revolut Technologies Inc. as technology services provider/program manager.

Group entity Revolut Group Holdings Ltd (UK company no. 12743269); Revolut Bank UK Ltd (no. 12871051) is authorised by the PRA and regulated by the FCA/PRA (FRN 981170); Revolut Ltd is FCA-authorised as an e-money institution (FRN 900562).

Global HQ opened in London's Canary Wharf (Sept 2025) and a Western Europe HQ in Paris (announced May 2025); EU banking is anchored in Lithuania, with ECB approval (Oct 2026) to transfer part of the Lithuanian bank's operations to a French bank entity (licensed Aug 2026) covering France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Portugal and Spain.

Founded in London in 2015 by Nik Storonsky and Vlad Yatsenko; grew from a money-transfer app into a financial services platform with banking operations across Europe and new banks launched in the UK, Mexico, Australia and New Zealand in 2026.

traction.claim: Company claim (audited annual report): 68.3 million retail customers at end-2025, up 30% YoY from 52.5M, with 16 million new customers added in 2025.
Company claim: more than 80 million retail customers across 40+ countries as of November 2026 (company website also says 80M+).
Company claim: 767K business customers at end-2025, up 33% YoY (2024: 578K); management targets 1 million businesses by 2027.
Company claim: total customer balances £50.2B ($67.5B) at end-2025, up 66% YoY; savings balances £20.4B, more than doubling YoY.
Company claim: total transaction volumes rose 65% YoY to $1.7 trillion in 2025; Revolut Business processed $365B of volume, growing over 140% YoY in Singapore, Australia and the US.

Revolut launched full banking operations in Mexico on 27 Jan 2026 — its first bank outside Europe and the first independent digital bank to obtain a Mexican licence via direct application; company claim: 1 million Mexican customers within eight months.

Partnerships: title partnership of the Audi Revolut F1 Team, Manchester City back-of-shirt sponsor with co-branded cards, Revolut Pay partnerships with Booking.com and Vueling, Visa powering first India cards, Mastercard as Mexico issuing partner, Vodafone network for Revolut Mobile in Ireland.
Company claim: 13 million customers in the UK, 6 million in Spain (where it says it is the 4th-largest bank by penetration with 13% share) and 5 million in France.

Regulatory traction in 2026: UK bank fully launched March 2026, banks launched in Mexico, Australia and New Zealand (NZ licence 3 Nov 2026), banking licences secured in France, Colombia and Argentina (Banco Cetelem acquisition approved Sept 2026).
Company claim: India rollout began 2026 with 350K+ waitlisted users and a target of 20 million Indian customers by 2030; company targets 100 million customers globally by mid-2027.

red_flags.claim: Repeat AML enforcement history in its main EU jurisdiction: a €3.5M Bank of Lithuania fine in April 2025 on top of three earlier fines/warnings in 2022-2024, showing persistent anti-money-laundering control weaknesses.

Recurring data-security incidents: the September 2022 breach exposing 50,150 customers' data (GDPR probe opened) was followed by the September 2026 accidental disclosure of customer data to hackers posing as government investigators.

Fraud exposure: most-complained-about UK firm for fraud and scam complaints to the Financial Ombudsman in 2024 and Jan-Aug 2025, with a BBC Panorama finding of ~10,000 Action Fraud complaints naming Revolut in 2023.
Audit-history risk: auditor BDO warned in 2023 that Revolut's IT system design risked the bulk of its 2021 revenue being materially misstated.
Governance/geography signal: founder-CEO Storonsky (owner of >25%) moved his residence from the UK to the UAE in October 2024 while the company is headquartered and regulated in London.

Valuation risk: the $115B mark (up from $33B in 2021) comes entirely from secondary share sales with no new capital into the company, and the private valuation exceeds Barclays and Société Générale despite much lower revenue per customer and a 6% loan-to-deposit ratio.

Sanctions-driven mass account closures for Russian/Belarusian clients (effective 31 Dec 2025) drew complaints that customers were earlier assured accounts were safe, a trust and conduct risk around sanctions implementation.

reputation.claim: Revolut recorded the highest number of fraud and scam complaints escalated to the UK Financial Ombudsman Service of any UK payment firm: 3,242 APP-fraud complaints in 2024 (vs Monzo 2,344, Barclays 1,704) and 1,875 in Jan–Aug 2025 with a 30% uphold rate; it led non-APP fraud complaints too (2,631 in 2024).

A BBC Panorama investigation found Revolut was named in almost 10,000 complaints to Action Fraud in 2023, more than any other major UK bank; PSR data shows £756 of every £1m received into Revolut consumer accounts was APP-scam related in 2023, above high-street peers.
Complaint pattern: customers report accounts frozen without explanation with funds locked for weeks or months, automated chatbot-only support with no phone line, and disputed fraud reimbursements.

Company-cited ratings: Trustpilot 4.7 (March 2026), 4.9 App Store, 4.8 Google Play (end-2025); contrast: the unclaimed app.revolut.com Trustpilot profile shows TrustScore 2.0/5 from 16 reviews — small-sample aggregator data, not representative per Trustpilot.

Employee/press sentiment: eFinancialCareers describes Revolut jobs as 'infamously intense' with people tending not to stay long; a Portuguese trade union reported employee complaints of abusive labour practices and 'unrealistic' metrics among ~1,200 Portugal staff (company says it complies with labour law).
Awards (company claim): Euromoney World's Best Digital Bank 2025, Global Finance Best Digital Bank 2025, named in Forbes World's Best Banks; certified Great Place to Work in 14 countries.

missing_fields: Independent/analyst revenue or profit estimates (all financials found are company-reported or press-cited annual-report figures)
Outcome and any sanction of the 2022 Lithuanian GDPR investigation into the data breach (regulator page states investigation opened, no result)
Current FCA/PRA enforcement docket or open supervisory actions (no live UK enforcement action found in collected sources; 2019 FCA AML investigation outcome not confirmed)
Named enterprise customer list beyond partnership announcements (Booking.com, Vueling, Audi F1, Manchester City)

Executive departures in the last 2 years beyond the November 2026 Revolut Business sales-role exits (e.g. no confirmed C-suite exits found in collected sources; the last major named departure found was the US boss in December 2021, outside the 2-year window)

financial_signals.claim: Company claim (FY2025 annual report): revenue $6.0B (£4.5B), up 46% YoY from $4.0B (£3.1B); profit before tax $2.3B (£1.7B), up 57%, PBT margin 38%; net profit $1.7B (£1.3B) — fifth consecutive year of profitability.
Company claim (FY2024 annual report): revenue £3.1B ($4.0B), up 72% YoY; profit before tax £1,089M, up 149%; net profit £790M; net profit margin 26%.
Headcount trend: 8,152 employees at end-2023, 10,133 at end-2024 (annual report), 12,200 at end-2025; ~12,000 globally as of March 2026 per Reuters.

Offshoring: ~40% of the global workforce to be based in India by end-2026, with 1,600 India roles filled in 2026 taking India headcount to 5,500; £500M committed to the India business over five years.

Hiring (company claim): 1.7 million job applications in 2025; plans for 1,000 high-skilled UK roles within a £3B UK investment and 400+ Western Europe roles; average headcount grew 10% YoY while risk & compliance headcount grew 42%.

November 2026: staff reductions via performance reviews — dozens departing, primarily Revolut Business sales roles in the UK and European offices; company says exits align with routine quarterly assessments, not a formal layoff program; reports of ~15,000 employees overall.
Balance sheet (company claim): total assets/balance sheet £43B, up 66%; total capital resources £4.9B, all CET1; loan-to-deposit ratio 6.2%; lending portfolio +120% to £2.2B.

AI cost push: Revolut is shifting coding for ~2,000 engineers from Claude/Codex to self-hosted open-weight models on ~56 Nvidia B200 GPUs, reporting ~90% lower inference costs and ~60% faster coding time.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: The Bank of Lithuania fined Revolut Bank UAB €3.5 million (~$3.83M) on 8 April 2025 for money-laundering-prevention failures — violations and shortcomings in monitoring business relationships and transactions — the largest penalty the central bank has ever issued; Revolut signed a settlement (administrative agreement) and says no confirmed instances of money laundering were identified.

Prior Bank of Lithuania enforcement against Revolut Bank UAB: €200,000 fine (23 Jan 2024, breach of Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 Art. 395(1)); €70,000 fine, warning and public disclosure (10 Nov 2022, payments-law and reporting violations); €50,000 fine and warning (15 Mar 2022, AML/customer-information violations).

A September 2022 cyberattack via social engineering exposed data of 50,150 customers worldwide (20,687 in the EEA, 379 in Lithuania) — names, addresses, emails, phone numbers and partial card data; Lithuania's State Data Protection Inspectorate opened a GDPR investigation on 20 Sept 2022 (outcome not stated on the regulator's page).
September 2026: Revolut accidentally sent customer data to hackers posing as government investigators; the company said its systems and customer funds were unaffected.
In 2019 the UK Financial Conduct Authority investigated Revolut for failing to comply with its anti-money-laundering systems (cited as context in City A.M. coverage of the 2025 Lithuanian fine).
In 2023 auditor BDO warned that the design of Revolut's IT system created a risk that the bulk of its 2021 revenue had been 'materially misstated'.

UK banking licence was granted with restrictions in July 2024 ('Authorisation with Restrictions'/mobilisation); the PRA lifted the restrictions and Revolut Bank UK launched full banking operations in March 2026.

Sanctions exposure/compliance: under the EU's 19th sanctions package (in effect 23 Oct 2025), Revolut began closing accounts of Russian and Belarusian citizens without valid EU/EEA residence or citizenship, with contracts terminated on 31 December 2025; Revolut says it must comply with UN, EU, UK and US sanctions laws.

US charter: Revolut received conditional approval from the OCC (3 Sept 2026) to establish a national bank, targeted to launch in H1 2027 subject to final approval; a formal charter application was filed with the OCC and FDIC in March 2026 (Revolut Bank US, N.A.).

In 2019 a Lithuanian parliament committee chair alleged Kremlin links (Storonsky's father's role at a Gazprom division; DST Global among shareholders) and called for an investigation that could have revoked its Lithuanian licence; Lithuanian committees concluded there were no Russian political connections at Revolut, and Storonsky renounced his Russian citizenship in October 2022.
